extracted.intended_audience: users of GAP (computational algebra system), mathematicians and programmers needing reference for vector/matrix functions
extracted.subtask_description: Reference-manual section documenting GAP operations on coefficient lists, vectors as polynomial coefficients, coding-theory utilities, and matrix constructors/attributes/algorithms. Specifies required argument conditions, return values, mutability, and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: LeftShiftRowVector
rubrics_metrics.description: LeftShiftRowVector(list, shift): changes list by assigning list[i] := list[i+shift] and removing the last shift entries of the result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operation mutates the given list by shifting contents left; trailing positions are removed. No example provided in this chunk.

rubrics_metrics.name: RightShiftRowVector
rubrics_metrics.description: RightShiftRowVector(list, shift, fill): changes list by assigning list[i+shift] := list[i] and filling each of the first shift entries with fill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operation mutates the given list by shifting contents right and inserting fill values into initial positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: ShrinkRowVector
rubrics_metrics.description: ShrinkRowVector(list): removes trailing zeroes from the list list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: l:=[1,0,0];;ShrinkRowVector(l); l; yields [1]. Removes only trailing zeroes.

rubrics_metrics.name: RemoveOuterCoeffs
rubrics_metrics.description: RemoveOuterCoeffs(list, coef): removes coef at the beginning and at the end of list and returns the number of elements removed at the beginning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: l:=[1,1,2,1,2,1,1,2,1];; RemoveOuterCoeffs(l,1); returns 2 and modifies l to [2,1,2,1,1,2].

rubrics_metrics.name: WeightVecFFE
rubrics_metrics.description: WeightVecFFE(vec): returns the weight of the finite field vector vec, i.e. the number of nonzero entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for coding-theory computations on vectors over finite fields; requires vector elements in a common finite field.

rubrics_metrics.name: DistanceVecFFE
rubrics_metrics.description: DistanceVecFFE(vec1, vec2): returns the distance between vec1 and vec2, the number of places where they differ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: vec1 and vec2 must have the same length and elements in a common field.

rubrics_metrics.name: DistancesDistributionVecFFEsVecFFE
rubrics_metrics.description: DistancesDistributionVecFFEsVecFFE(vecs, vec): returns the distances distribution of vec to vectors in list vecs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All vectors must have same length and entries in a common field. Returns list d of length Length(vec)+1 where d[i] is the number of vectors in vecs at distance i+1 to vec.

rubrics_metrics.name: DistancesDistributionMatFFEVecFFE
rubrics_metrics.description: DistancesDistributionMatFFEVecFFE(mat, F, vec): returns the distances distribution of vec to the vectors in the vector space generated by rows of mat over finite field F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Row length must equal Length(vec); all entries must lie in F; rows of mat must be linearly independent. Returns list d of length Length(vec)+1 where d[i] counts vectors at distance i+1.

rubrics_metrics.name: AClosestVectorCombinationsMatFFEVecFFE / AClosestVectorCombinationsMatFFEVecFFECoords
rubrics_metrics.description: These functions enumerate f-linear combinations of rows of mat that use exactly cnt rows and find the vector closest to vec among them; may stop early if distance ≤ stop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments require rows and vec of same length and elements in field f; rows of mat must be linearly independent. AClosestVectorCombinationsMatFFE returns the closest vector; AClosest...Coords returns [closest_vector, v] where v has exactly cnt non-zero entries and v*mat equals the closest vector.

rubrics_metrics.name: CosetLeadersMatFFE
rubrics_metrics.description: CosetLeadersMatFFE(mat, f): returns a list of representatives of minimal weight for the cosets of a code defined by check matrix mat over finite field f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: mat must be a check matrix; all rows same length and elements in f; rows must be linearly independent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vectors as coefficients of polynomials (section guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists of ring elements can be treated as coefficient lists of polynomials or as row vectors; the following operations perform arithmetic on univariate polynomials given by coefficient lists which must be dense homogeneous lists over a commutative ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists can differ in length; not all input lists may be empty. If length parameters leni omitted, they default to the list lengths. Coefficient of x^i is at position i+1.

rubrics_metrics.name: ValuePol
rubrics_metrics.description: ValuePol(coeff, x): given coeff as coefficient list of f and ring element x, returns f(x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coefficient of x^i stored at position i+1. Example: ValuePol([1,2,3],4) returns 57.

rubrics_metrics.name: ProductCoeffs
rubrics_metrics.description: ProductCoeffs(list1[, len1], list2[, len2]): returns the coefficient list of the product of polynomials p1 and p2 given by the first len1/len2 entries of list1/list2 (defaults to full lengths).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ProductCoeffs([1,2,3,4],[5,6,7]) returns [5,16,34,52,45,28].

rubrics_metrics.name: ReduceCoeffs
rubrics_metrics.description: ReduceCoeffs(list1[, len1], list2[, len2]): changes list1 to the coefficient list of the remainder when dividing p1 by p2; returns position of last non-zero entry but may not remove trailing zeroes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: list1 must be mutable. Example: ReduceCoeffs([1,2,3,4],[5,6,7]) returns 2 and modifies l to [64/49, -24/49, 0, 0].

rubrics_metrics.name: ReduceCoeffsMod
rubrics_metrics.description: ReduceCoeffsMod(list1[, len1], list2[, len2], modulus): changes list1 to coefficient list of remainder when dividing p1 by p2 modulo modulus (positive integer); returns position of last non-zero entry but may not remove trailing zeroes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: list1 must be mutable. Example: ReduceCoeffsMod([1,2,3,4],[5,6,7],3) returns 1 and modifies l to [1,0,0,0].

rubrics_metrics.name: PowerModCoeffs
rubrics_metrics.description: PowerModCoeffs(list1[, len1], exp, list2[, len2]): returns coefficient list of remainder when dividing p1^exp by p2; coefficients are reduced during powering to avoid explosion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: len defaults to list lengths. Example: PowerModCoeffs([1,2,3,4],5,[5,6,7]) returns given rational coefficients (example in manual).

rubrics_metrics.name: ShiftedCoeffs
rubrics_metrics.description: ShiftedCoeffs(list, shift): produces new coefficient list new with new[i+shift] := list[i] and fills initial holes with zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not mutate original. Examples: ShiftedCoeffs([1,2,3],2) -> [0,0,1,2,3]; ShiftedCoeffs([1,2,3],-2) -> [3].

rubrics_metrics.name: InfoMatrix
rubrics_metrics.description: InfoMatrix: the info class for matrix operations is InfoMatrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for logging/info categorization of matrix operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsMatrix
rubrics_metrics.description: IsMatrix(obj): by convention a matrix is a list of lists of equal length whose entries lie in a common ring; in GAP IsMatrix is a synonym for a table of ring elements (IsTable and IsRingElement), so it may return true for non-rectangular tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To test rectangularness use IsRectangularTable. Examples show IsMatrix([[1,2],[3]]) returns true but IsRectangularTable([[1,2],[3]]) returns false. Empty structures like [] or [[]] are not matrices; IsMatrix([[]]) returns false.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsOrdinaryMatrix
rubrics_metrics.description: IsOrdinaryMatrix(obj): category for matrices whose multiplication is ordinary matrix multiplication. Each matrix in internal representation is in IsOrdinaryMatrix; arithmetic preserves this category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes between different matrix multiplications so product applicability and result types are well-defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsLieMatrix
rubrics_metrics.description: IsLieMatrix(mat): category for matrices whose multiplication is given by the Lie bracket; matrices created by LieObject are in IsLieMatrix and arithmetic preserves this category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lie matrices behave like ordinary matrices except with different multiplication; must be distinguished from ordinary matrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix arithmetic rules (operators)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions of +, -, *, /, ^, Comm, scalar/matrix interactions, vec*mat, mat*vec, mat1*mat2, and list-of-matrices operations specifying expected operand shapes, common-field requirements, and typical results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most usual situations assume compatible dimensions and common field; in general mixing types may produce tables of mixed elements. Left/right division defined using inverse. Powering by integer or invertible matrix described (integer powers, conjugation by invertible matrix). Many list-level variants (scalar + matlist, mat * matlist, vec * matlist) are defined with elementwise semantics; see mutability note (12.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: DimensionsMat
rubrics_metrics.description: DimensionsMat(mat) (attribute): returns [#rows, #columns] for mat; returns fail if mat is not a IsRectangularTable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: DimensionsMat([[1,2,3],[4,5,6]]) -> [2,3]; DimensionsMat([[1,2,3],[4,5]]) -> fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: DefaultFieldOfMatrix
rubrics_metrics.description: DefaultFieldOfMatrix(mat) (attribute): returns either a field containing all entries of mat or fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For matrices of finite field elements or cyclotomics returns the default field generated by entries. Example: DefaultFieldOfMatrix([[Z(4),Z(8)]]) -> GF(2^6).

rubrics_metrics.name: TraceMatrix / TraceMat / Trace
rubrics_metrics.description: TraceMatrix(mat): the trace of a square matrix is the sum of its diagonal entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute synonyms exist (TraceMat, Trace). Example: TraceMatrix([[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]]) -> 15.

rubrics_metrics.name: DeterminantMatrix / DeterminantMat / Determinant
rubrics_metrics.description: DeterminantMatrix(mat): returns determinant of square matrix mat; methods assume mat over an integral domain whose quotient field is implemented in GAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For matrices over arbitrary commutative rings see DeterminantMatDivFree.

rubrics_metrics.name: DeterminantMatrixDestructive / DeterminantMatDestructive
rubrics_metrics.description: Destructive variant: same as DeterminantMatrix but may destroy its argument; mat must be mutable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows matrix mm mutated after call; destructive variant can be more memory/time efficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: DeterminantMatrixDivFree / DeterminantMatDivFree
rubrics_metrics.description: DeterminantMatrixDivFree(mat): returns determinant of square matrix over arbitrary commutative ring using the division-free method of Mahajan and Vinay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when quotient field not available or to avoid division.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsEmptyMatrix
rubrics_metrics.description: IsEmptyMatrix(M) (property): returns true if matrix object M has zero columns or zero rows (i.e., no entries), false otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to test 'empty' matrix objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsMonomialMatrix
rubrics_metrics.description: IsMonomialMatrix(mat) (property): true iff mat has exactly one nonzero entry in every row and every column.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: IsMonomialMatrix([[0,1],[1,0]]) -> true.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsDiagonalMatrix / IsDiagonalMat
rubrics_metrics.description: IsDiagonalMatrix(mat): returns true if mat has only zero entries off the main diagonal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided; returns false for permutation matrix [[0,1],[1,0]].

rubrics_metrics.name: IsUpperTriangularMatrix / IsUpperTriangularMat
rubrics_metrics.description: IsUpperTriangularMatrix(mat): returns true if mat has only zero entries below the main diagonal.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsLowerTriangularMatrix / IsLowerTriangularMat
rubrics_metrics.description: IsLowerTriangularMatrix(mat): returns true if mat has only zero entries above the main diagonal.

rubrics_metrics.name: IdentityMat
rubrics_metrics.description: IdentityMat(m[, R]) returns a mutable m×m identity matrix over ring R (or element of a ring); defaults to integer matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: IdentityMat(3) yields 3x3 identity; IdentityMat(2, Integers mod 15) yields identity in Zmod 15; IdentityMat accepts ring element to determine base domain.

rubrics_metrics.name: NullMat
rubrics_metrics.description: NullMat(m, n[, R]) returns a mutable m×n null (zero) matrix over ring R; defaults to integer matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples shown for integers, ZmodnZ, and finite field zero elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: EmptyMatrix (constructor)
rubrics_metrics.description: EmptyMatrix(char): returns an empty (ordinary) matrix in characteristic char that can be added to or multiplied with empty lists and acts on lists representing zero-dimensional row vectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: EmptyMatrix(5) prints as EmptyMatrix(5); AsList(last) -> [].

rubrics_metrics.name: DiagonalMat
rubrics_metrics.description: DiagonalMat(vector): returns a diagonal matrix with diagonal entries given by vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: DiagonalMat([1,2,3]) -> diagonal matrix with 1,2,3 on diagonal.

rubrics_metrics.name: DiagonalMatrix (with base domain)
rubrics_metrics.description: DiagonalMatrix([filt,] R, vector) or DiagonalMatrix(vector[, M]) returns square matrix or matrix object with diagonal entries from vector and off-diagonals zero; optional semiring R sets base domain; optional filt chooses internal representation; optional matrix M sets representation and base domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If ConstructingFilter implies IsCopyable result will be fully mutable. Examples show various usages producing matrices over GF(9), Rationals, Integers, or plain lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: PermutationMat
rubrics_metrics.description: PermutationMat(perm, dim[, F]) returns a matrix in dimension dim over field given by F representing permutation perm acting by permuting basis vectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: PermutationMat((1,2,3),4,1) returns 4x4 permutation matrix with permutation on first three basis vectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: TransposedMatImmutable / TransposedMat / TransposedMatMutable / TransposedMatOp
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the transpose of matrix object mat. They differ in mutability: TransposedMat (and TransposedMatImmutable) return immutable result; TransposedMatMutable (and TransposedMatOp) return a mutable matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TransposedMat is attribute and returns immutable result. Use TransposedMatMutable to guarantee a new mutable matrix.

rubrics_metrics.name: TransposedMatDestructive
rubrics_metrics.description: TransposedMatDestructive(mat): if mat is mutable, computes transpose by swapping entries in mat, modifying mat in place; otherwise behaves like TransposedMat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows mm mutated to its transpose after call.

rubrics_metrics.name: KroneckerProduct
rubrics_metrics.description: KroneckerProduct(mat1, mat2): returns Kronecker product where each entry a of mat1 is replaced by a*mat2.

rubrics_metrics.name: ReflectionMat
rubrics_metrics.description: ReflectionMat(coeffs[, conj][, root]) returns matrix of the reflection in vector with coefficients coeffs; optional root (root of unity) determines order; optional conj is conjugation function (default ComplexConjugate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflection defined as M = I_n + conj(vtr) * (root-1)/(v·conj(vtr)) * v. Default root gives reflection of order 2 (maps v to -v); triflections possible with third root of unity. conj defaults to ComplexConjugate.

rubrics_metrics.name: PrintArray
rubrics_metrics.description: PrintArray(array): pretty-prints the array.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility for display formatting of arrays.

rubrics_metrics.name: RandomMat
rubrics_metrics.description: RandomMat([rs,] m, n[, R]) returns a new mutable random m×n matrix with elements taken from ring R (defaults to Integers); optional random source rs may be supplied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: RandomMat(2,3,GF(3)) shows entries in GF(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: RandomInvertibleMat
rubrics_metrics.description: RandomInvertibleMat([rs,] m[, R]) returns a new mutable random invertible m×m matrix with elements from R (defaults to Integers); optional rs allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows a 4x4 random invertible integer matrix and its inverse.

rubrics_metrics.name: RandomUnimodularMat
rubrics_metrics.description: RandomUnimodularMat([rs,] m) returns a random mutable m×m integer matrix invertible over the integers; optional rs; option domain may restrict sampling domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows unimodular matrices and their integer inverses; large-domain sampling example given.

rubrics_metrics.name: RankMatrix / RankMat
rubrics_metrics.description: RankMatrix(mat): returns the dimension of the free module spanned by rows if the rows span a free module over ring generated by entries and inverses; otherwise fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May perform Gaussian elimination; large rational matrices can be slow due to large intermediate entries. Example: RankMatrix of [[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]] returns 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: TriangulizedMat / RREF (attribute)
rubrics_metrics.description: TriangulizedMat(mat) / RREF(mat): computes an upper triangular form / reduced row echelon form of mat via Gaussian algorithm and returns a mutable upper triangular matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synonym RREF exists. The result is mutable and sometimes called Hermite normal form.

rubrics_metrics.name: TriangulizeMat (destructive)
rubrics_metrics.description: TriangulizeMat(mat): applies Gaussian algorithm to mutable matrix mat and changes it to upper triangular normal form (Hermite normal form / RREF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mutates given matrix; example shows mm changed to triangular form.

rubrics_metrics.name: NullspaceMat / TriangulizedNullspaceMat
rubrics_metrics.description: NullspaceMat(mat) returns an immutable matrix whose rows are a basis of solutions to vec * mat = 0; TriangulizedNullspaceMat returns basis in triangulized form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The basis is not guaranteed to be in any specific form unless TriangulizedNullspaceMat variant is used. Example: NullspaceMat of example returns [[1,-2,1]].

rubrics_metrics.name: NullspaceMatDestructive / TriangulizedNullspaceMatDestructive
rubrics_metrics.description: Destructive variants compute the same as their non-destructive counterparts but may destroy mat to save memory; mat must be mutable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows mm mutated after NullspaceMatDestructive.

rubrics_metrics.name: SolutionMat
rubrics_metrics.description: SolutionMat(mat, vec): returns a row vector x that is a solution to x * mat = vec; returns fail if no solution exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: SolutionMat(mat,[3,5,7]) -> [5/3,1/3,0].

rubrics_metrics.name: SolutionMatDestructive
rubrics_metrics.description: SolutionMatDestructive(mat, vec): same as SolutionMat but may destroy mat and vec; mat must be mutable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows both mm and v destroyed (v becomes zero vector) after call.

rubrics_metrics.name: BaseFixedSpace
rubrics_metrics.description: BaseFixedSpace(mats): returns list of row vectors that form a basis of vector space V such that v*M = v for all M in mats (common eigenspace for eigenvalue 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: BaseFixedSpace([[[1,2],[0,1]]]) -> [[0,1]].

rubrics_metrics.name: GeneralisedEigenvalues / GeneralizedEigenvalues
rubrics_metrics.description: GeneralisedEigenvalues(F, A): computes the generalized eigenvalues of matrix A over field F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operation name has US/UK spelling synonyms; used for eigenvalue computations over specified field.

rubrics_metrics.name: GeneralisedEigenspaces / GeneralizedEigenspaces
rubrics_metrics.description: GeneralisedEigenspaces(F, A): computes generalized eigenspaces of A over field F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: US/UK synonyms provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eigenvalues
rubrics_metrics.description: Eigenvalues(F, A): returns eigenvalues of matrix A over field F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard eigenvalue computation over specified field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eigenspaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Eigenspaces(F, A): returns eigenspaces of matrix A over field F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard eigenspace computation over specified field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eigenvectors
rubrics_metrics.description: Eigenvectors(F, A): returns eigenvectors of matrix A over field F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard eigenvector computation over specified field.

rubrics_metrics.name: ElementaryDivisorsMat
rubrics_metrics.description: ElementaryDivisorsMat([ring,] mat): returns list of elementary divisors d such that d[i] divides d[i+1] and mat is equivalent to diagonal matrix with d[i] on diagonal; operations performed over euclidean ring 'ring' which must contain matrix entries (defaults to DefaultRing of entries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ElementaryDivisorsMat(mat) -> [1,3,0]. Works for polynomial-matrix examples when ring is a polynomial ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: ElementaryDivisorsMatDestructive
rubrics_metrics.description: Destructive variant may destroy contents of mat while producing same elementary divisors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when memory saving is desirable and mat is mutable.

rubrics_metrics.name: ElementaryDivisorsTransformationsMat / ElementaryDivisorsTransformationsMatDestructive
rubrics_metrics.description: ElementaryDivisorsTransformationsMat([ring,] mat): like ElementaryDivisorsMat but also calculates transforming matrices; returns record with components normal (S), rowtrans (P), coltrans (Q) such that P * A * Q = S. Destructive variant destroys mat contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operations performed over euclidean ring 'ring' (defaults to DefaultRing of entries). Large example provided showing returned record and validation P*mat*Q = normal.

rubrics_metrics.name: DiagonalizeMat
rubrics_metrics.description: DiagonalizeMat(ring, mat): brings mutable matrix mat (over ring) into diagonal form by elementary row and column operations, mutating mat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: DiagonalizeMat(Integers, [[1,2],[2,1]]) yields [[1,0],[0,3]] after mutation.

rubrics_metrics.name: SemiEchelonMat
rubrics_metrics.description: SemiEchelonMat(mat) (attribute): for a matrix over a field F, semi-echelon form has first nonzero element in each row equal to identity of F and zeros directly below pivots; SemiEchelonMat returns a record with information about semi-echelonized form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Component details of returned record not included in this chunk; this documents the notion of semi-echelon used by GAP.
